key_evidence_accepted: The Supreme Court accepted that the shelf life of the insecticide had expired prior to the filing of the complaint, rendering further test and analysis by the Central Insecticides Laboratory impossible.
witness_credibility: The court assessed that the accused had notified its intention to adduce evidence in controversion of the report, which took the report out of the class of 'conclusive evidence' and conferred the right to have the sample tested by the Central Insecticides Laboratory.

legal_representation.state: P.K. Dey, Rashmi Malhotra, Rohitash S. Nagar, R.S. Nagar, D.S. Mehra, B.V. Balaram Das

investigation_status: Complaint filed against the appellant and its dealer under Section 29 of the Insecticides Act. Shelf life of the insecticide expired before the complaint was filed. Application for discharge under Section 245 CrPC dismissed by the Chief Judicial Magistrate. Order upheld by the High Court in Criminal Revision.

appeal_history.trial_court: Application for discharge under Section 245 CrPC dismissed by the Chief Judicial Magistrate
appeal_history.high_court: Criminal Revision No. 170 of 2000 dismissed by the High Court
appeal_history.supreme_court: Appeal allowed, impugned judgments set aside, appellant discharged of criminal liability

prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the accused failed to specifically request the sample to be sent for analysis to the Central Insecticides Laboratory, thereby defeating their right to re-analysis, and that the shelf life of the insecticide had expired before the complaint was filed, making further analysis futile.
defence_argument: The defence argued that merely notifying the intention to adduce evidence in controversion of the report was sufficient to invoke the right to re-analysis by the Central Insecticides Laboratory, and that the shelf life of the insecticide had expired, rendering further analysis impossible and the prosecution futile.
legal_principle_applied: The legal principle applied was that notifying the intention to adduce evidence in controversion of the report of the Insecticide Analyst removes the report's conclusive nature and confers the right to re-analysis by the Central Insecticides Laboratory, without requiring a specific demand for such analysis.
precedent_relied_upon: State of Haryana v. Unique Farmaid (P) Ltd. & Ors. (1999) 8 SCC 190; State of Punjab v. National Organic Chemical Industries Ltd. (1997) SCC (Crl.) 312; Mis. Gupta Chemicals Pvt.' Ltd. & Ors. v. State of Rajasthan & Anr. JT 2002 (Suppl.1) SC 516
other_sentence_order: The appellant was discharged of its criminal liability.
